# espalier — `docs/`

These are not notes about the implementation. They are the specification, and
where the code and one of them disagree the document is right — so a behaviour
change is a change here first, and a document that is ambiguous or
self-contradictory is something to report rather than to interpret.

Each covers one subject and says why, not only what. A decision recorded
without its reasoning is one that gets reversed by the next person who finds it
inconvenient.

**Write the design, never the route to it.** A page here says what the tool is
and why it is that, in the present tense, with no trace of what it was before.
"This reverses an earlier position", "previous releases did X", "an earlier
draft said Y" — all of it goes. The reader has no idea what the earlier position
was, cannot see the draft, and gains nothing from being told a decision was hard
to reach; they are trying to use the thing. A history wearing the clothes of a
specification also decays badly, because the past keeps accumulating while the
statement stays the same size.

The reasoning is not the history. "One walk, in one language, is what a linter
can explain" is an argument and belongs here. "Earlier releases shelled out to
git" is a changelog and does not. When cutting a passage of the second kind,
keep the first kind that was buried in it.

`HANDOFF.MD` at the root is where the route belongs, and it keeps superseded
decisions struck through rather than deleted. It is read by whoever inherits
this project; these pages are read by whoever is using it.

## Project layout

    docs/
    ├─ cli/         one page per command
    │
    ├─ API.MD       using espalier as a library (required)
    │
    ├─ CONFIG.MD    the configuration file and the ignore list (required)
    │
    ├─ ERRORS.MD    every operational failure and what it means (required)
    │
    ├─ MATCHING.MD  how a rule module claims a file (required)
    │
    └─ TYPES.MD     what a rule module exports and receives (required)

## `API.MD` — using espalier as a library

Covers the package: what it exports, what those functions return, and what a
caller must build to test a rule. A rule module's own contract is TYPES.MD;
this is the other side of that boundary.

## `CONFIG.MD` — the configuration file and the ignore list

Covers `espalier.config.yaml` and `.espalierignore`: every key, how the root is
discovered, where a child espalier's authority begins, and what is excluded
from the walk. How a declared path claims a file is MATCHING.MD.

## `ERRORS.MD` — every operational failure and what it means

One table, every code reported with `kind: "failure"`. A code `fail()` raises
that this does not list fails the suite, and so does a code listed here that
nothing raises — the table is checked in both directions on purpose.

## `MATCHING.MD` — how a rule module claims a file

Covers the espalier tree: how a path inside it becomes a pattern, which pattern
owns a file when several could, and what must exist. What a module exports is
TYPES.MD; what a command does with the answer is its page under `docs/cli/`.

## `TYPES.MD` — what a rule module exports and receives

Covers the contract between a rule module and the runner: every export a module
may declare, and every field of the context its `lint` is handed. Where such a
file may sit, and which files it claims, is MATCHING.MD.

## Constraints

### Markdown files

These rules apply to all Markdown files under this directory.

#### document-heading — every document opens with a level-one heading

Opens with a level-one heading naming its subject. A
document a reader lands in the middle of should say what it is before it says
anything else.

## Other repository paths

These paths are part of the repository but serve specific purposes outside the project layout. Use them only for the purpose stated here.

| Paths | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `AGENTS.MD` | Generated repository guidance; edits here will be overwritten. Modify [`ESPALIER.MD`](../espalier/docs/ESPALIER.MD) to change this document's persistent guidance. |

Every path under docs/ must fit the project layout or a documented
repository-specific purpose.
